title: In-house synthesizability-constrained de novo design yields an MGLL-active ligand
summary: A multi-objective generative workflow used a retrainable in-house synthesizability score and a QSAR model to design monoglyceride lipase (MGLL) ligands that can be made from about 6000 in-house building blocks. CASP success fell by only 12% when accepting routes two steps longer. Three de novo candidates were synthesised and one showed evident MGLL activity; activity values were not read.
ai_technology: Multi-objective generative de novo design with a retrainable in-house synthesizability score and QSAR model

evidence.tested: Three candidates synthesised via CASP routes and tested in a biochemical assay.
evidence.unknown: Activity values; only one of three candidates was active; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Generative design proposed the synthesizable ligands.
